I'm in the military, and this episode has confirmed that I'm going to have a bit of a love-hate relationship with GATE. On one hand, I get to see glorious FIYAPOWAH applied liberally and then some. On the other hand, the silly Hollywood Tactics are going to be the death of me, particularly in some of the jargon. Oh, crucified Christ, where to begin?

  1. This is a holdover from last episode, but one is not simply "promoted" to a commissioned rank. If, for whatever reason, you're selected for a commision, you go off to a months-long training school first because being an officer entails a lot of things, foremost among them being leading a lot of people in a tactical and administrative capacity. 3 months does not a butterbar make!
  2. Why do they have no intel? If they've been sending scouts through, why not have maps? Or ROEs? Or at least a general idea of "Yeah, there's shit on the other side!"
  3. At least they got the order of battle for an unexplored tunnel like this right. Tanks at front, APCs behind. Generally it'd be the inverse (let your APCs use their mobility, deploy troops, and then use tanks to support), but given circumstances it's tactically sound.
  4. Exposed infantry positions call for airburst fragmentation munitions, artillerymen! Ground bursts are for entrenched positions or structures!
  5. Barbed wire's a bit out of date. Try concertina!
  6. Did he just say no to a commanding officer?
  7. I get that this guy is lackadaisical with his job and whatnot, but mother of god is he a butterbar. Being laid-back is only a good thing if you know what you're doing and have the respect of your troops (Machiavellian "be feared and loved"), being laid-back because you're lazy just makes you a shitty lieutenant.
  8. Recon or Public Relations, pick one. Or, if you're gonna tack the latter onto the former, send someone who's trained to interact with civilians, not a butterbar!
  9. Okay, this is pretty hilarious. And pretty on-par for mission chatter.
  10. "All units, move out." Dude, you're one squad - you only have one unit.
  11. Perimeter security, numbnuts!

I gave up on associating legit military action with any form of media quite a while ago. I did chuckle when he said no to his CO though, I'd love to see someone say that so plainly to mine. Would be hilarious.
